content: Node streaming parse pattern: stream-json (official npm docs) parses JSON far larger than RAM with SAX-style pipeline; canonical example literally matches this use case: fs.createReadStream -> parser() -> pick({filter:'data'}) -> streamArray() emits one array element at a time in constant memory. unzipper (official npm docs) provides low-memory streaming unzip (zlib built-in, no native deps); Parse()/parseOne() pipe entries downstream; must autodrain unconsumed entries; buffer() exists for small entries. Avoid adm-zip/jszip (buffer whole archive in memory). Recommendation: download 8.7MB ZIP to memory/temp -> unzipper.Parse() entry '*.json' -> stream-json pick 'dados' + streamArray -> batch 1000 records -> never materialize the 225MB JSON or full object graph (which would be multi-GB).
